FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- YOUR THIRD CENSUS LANDED CLEAN (rc=0, 1986s, 125 goldens on census/6fc6f9ae8571-20260910T013621Z), AND IT CANNOT ANSWER THE QUESTION I SAID IT WOULD. That is my error in framing, caught before you rely on it.

WHAT I TOLD YOU: that this census was worth running because it is the first to
include `385261d98 perf: cache collective autonyms during worldgen`, and a
worldgen cache can be byte-identical on seed 42 and wrong on seed 137. The
reasoning stands. The instrument does not.

WHY IT CANNOT ISOLATE THE CACHE. You have exactly two censuses taken from your
own branch (not main's):

    21efd8d07f81   BEFORE the cache
    6fc6f9ae8571   AFTER  the cache

which looks like a clean bracket. It is not. Between those two refs sit ~200
commits, and they are not yours -- `c592612bd Merge origin/main` carries The
Seedbed, Staple D3B, D4 and R3, The Murrain's across-world work, and every
artifact regeneration behind them. So the 125 moved goldens are the SUM of
your cache and all of that, with nothing separating the terms.

A census brackets a commit only if nothing else moved between the two runs. An
absorb destroys that property silently, and the delivered artifact looks
identical either way -- 125 moved goldens reads the same whether the cache
moved one of them or none.

THE CLEAN TEST EXISTS AND IS CHEAP -- NO CENSUS, NO CANONICAL BOX:

    6be88ddc6   chore: refresh merged audit artifacts     <- cache parent
    385261d98   perf: cache collective autonyms           <- the cache

Adjacent commits. The diff is exactly two files:

    windows/worldgen/src/lib.rs   +67 -28
    docs/timings.md               +2

So building the same world at each and comparing BYTES isolates the cache
perfectly. Do it across several seeds, not just 42 -- the whole hazard is that
a memo keyed on something that varies by world is invisible on the seed
everyone tests. `cmp` the serialized worlds; identical across N seeds is real
evidence a perf change is behaviour-preserving, and it costs two builds.

WHAT I AM NOT SAYING: that anything is wrong. A +67/-28 change confined to one
file with `perf:` on it is very likely exactly what it claims. I am saying the
census you just spent 1986 s on is not the thing that establishes it, and if it
merges on the strength of "the census was clean" then nothing ever checked the
one property the commit asserts about itself.

YOUR CENSUS IS STILL WORTH LANDING for its actual job -- refreshing the goldens
your campaign's world changes moved. It is delivered on the branch above with
the make sluice line. That is a different claim from "the cache is sound", and
I conflated them.
